title: From data to meaning: Capturing expert interpretations for interdisciplinary data reuse with 3‐TIER
content:
ABSTRACT

Processing data for integrated Human and Earth System models is time-intensive, due to the data's complexity and required interdisciplinary dialog to make specialized datasets usable and accessible across disciplines. The Human and Earth System Coupled Research (HESCOR) project at the University of Cologne addressed this challenge by developing structured methods to lower barriers to interdisciplinary research and promote data sharing across academic fields. The approach, 3-Tiered Interpretation for Exchange and Reuse (3-TIER), is a three-tiered workflow implemented using CKAN (an open-source data-management system) that mirrors the movement of data from dataset discovery to contextualized reuse. Tier I provides uniform metadata for searchability and accessibility; Tier II reorganizes raw data using standardized terminology and quality metrics; and Tier III captures interpreted data. This structure encourages researchers to reflect on and communicate their interpretive choices across disciplinary boundaries, resulting in more transparent and reproducible modeling of the Human and Earth System. We identify four key lessons: (i) standardized metadata are critical for long-term data findability and usability; (ii) rigorous documentation compels researchers to interrogate their data, improving cross-disciplinary communication; (iii) infrastructure development presents a resource trade-off for new projects; and (iv) existing databases rarely house interpreted data. Because 3-TIER is data-agnostic, it offers a transferable framework for cross-disciplinary knowledge exchange, particularly in a modeling context. We recommend substantial reflection on data needs for projects during the application phase and the development of an interdisciplinary, data-focused research community.
